room.summary_lesson: Restoring access cannot take back information already stolen. Keep watching for new problems.

task_ui.hint: Take your time. Read the labels before choosing.

case.brief: The attacker is gone, but Anna's account is still a mess. Give it back to the real Anna, undo what the thief changed, change the locks on her other accounts, then check she can work again.
sample_evidence: Her account was used from an unknown computer.
The private payroll file was copied.
Information was sent outside the company.
sample_monitoring: Unexpected device and outbound traffic reported.
case.lesson: On your own account, use the provider's official recovery process and check your recovery details afterwards.

practice.title: Backup recovery practice
practice.brief: A separate practice incident has left a database unavailable. Response has contained the incident. Choose a trustworthy backup and verify that the restored data works.
practice.lesson: For photos or school files, a complete checked backup can help you recover lost data. A date alone does not prove a copy is safe.

password.title: Give Anna her account back
password.instruction: Two people asked the sign-in system to unlock Anna's account. Check each request against her HR record, then give her a strong new password.
password.lesson: Account recovery must prove who is asking. Then a long passphrase and a lock after a few wrong tries stop guessing.
password.full: Strong pick: four random words are long and hard to guess. Now lock the account after a few wrong tries.
password.success: Anna has her account back with a password that's hard to guess, and wrong guesses now lock it.
password.final_switch: Lock the account after 5 wrong tries

identity.record: HR record:  Anna Reyes  /  Staff 0419  /  Phone ...42  /  Works at the office

requests.title: REQUEST A
requests.name: Anna Reyes
requests.right: Rejected. The phone and place do not match her record: this was the thief trying to get back in.
requests.wrong: Look again: this phone ends in 97, not 42, and it came from Germany. That is not Anna.

requests.title: REQUEST B
requests.name: Anna Reyes
requests.right: Approved. Everything matches her HR record.
requests.wrong: Everything here matches her HR record. This is the real Anna.

password.identity_prompt: Compare each request with the HR record. Approve the real Anna, reject the other.
password.identity_done: Identity checked. Now pick Anna's new password.
password.choice_prompt: Pick the password that is hardest to guess.

choices.reason: Too easy: her name and the year are among the first things an attacker tries.
It looks tricky, but "P@ssw0rd!" is on every attacker's guess list.

settings.title: Undo the thief's changes
settings.instruction: The activity log shows every change to Anna's account. Undo what the thief did overnight; keep what Anna did herself.
settings.lesson: After a break-in, check what the attacker changed and put it back. Then add a second sign-in step so a stolen password is not enough.

items.reason: Anna did this herself from her office PC, before the attack. Leave it.

items.time: Sent all her email to a stranger

settings.pick: Undo every change made by the unknown computer. Keep what Anna did.
settings.remaining: {left} change(s) by the thief still need undoing.
settings.final_prompt: Everything the thief changed is undone. Now require 2-step sign-in so the stolen password alone can't get back in.
settings.final_switch_locked: Undo every change the thief made first.
settings.success: The thief's changes are gone, and a stolen password alone can no longer sign in.

reused.title: Change the locks
reused.instruction: The account manager lists Anna's other accounts. Try the stolen password on each one, then change it on every account it opens.
reused.lesson: Give every account its own password, so one stolen password opens only one door.

doors.name:
PAYROLL
PORTAL
doors.reason: The stolen key did not open this door. It already has its own password, so leave it.

doors.name:
BANK
APP
doors.reason: The stolen key did not open this door. It already has its own password, so leave it.

reused.pick: Drag the stolen key onto each door, or press the key and then a door.
reused.key_picked: Now press a door to try the key.
reused.opened: The stolen key opened {name}. Press the door to change its lock.
reused.held: The stolen key does not open {name}. It is safe.
reused.rekeyed: Lock changed. {left} door(s) the key opens still need a new lock.
reused.test_first: Try the stolen key on this door first.
reused.success: Every door the stolen key opened now has its own new lock.

file_server.title: Back to work
file_server.instruction: Test Anna's account on the file server the way she uses it every morning. Each step proves one repair worked.
file_server.lesson: Recovery is finished only when the person can work normally again and you have checked it.

checks.label: ANNA'S SIGN-IN
checks.expected: Trusted record: Anna should be able to sign in.
checks.passed: Anna signed in with her recovered account.
checks.failed: Anna still cannot sign in. Account recovery needs more help.

checks.label: RECOVERY CONTACT
checks.expected: Trusted record: the recovery contact belongs to Anna.
checks.passed: The account's recovery contact matches Anna's record.
checks.failed: The recovery contact does not match Anna's record. Report the mismatch.

checks.label: SHARED TEST FILE
checks.expected: Trusted record: an ordinary shared file should open.
checks.passed: The test file opened and its sample contents match.
checks.failed: The shared test file could not be verified. Do not mark recovery complete.

file_server.compare_again: Compare the staff record and account contact again. If they differ, report it and keep recovery open.
file_server.all_checks: Run every check before confirming recovery.
file_server.failed: A check failed. Keep recovery open and ask the response team to address the result.
file_server.success: Anna signed in, approved the code and opened her file. She is back to work.

prompts.sign_in: Sign Anna in with the new password you gave her.
prompts.code: 2-step sign-in sent a code to Anna's phone. Type it in.
prompts.test_file: Last, open the payroll report to check her files work.

file_server.wrong_digit: That digit does not match the phone. Start the code again.
file_server.wrong_file: That is not the payroll report.
file_server.file_opened: Payroll report opened. All 42 rows are there.

fails.sign_in: The passphrase is right, but sign-in still fails. Recovery needs more help.
fails.code: The code went to ...97, not Anna's phone. Report it: recovery stays open.
fails.test_file: The file would not open. Do not mark recovery complete.

sessions.title: Lock out the thief
sessions.instruction: The attacker signed in with Anna's stolen password. Sign out the devices that aren't hers, then turn on 2-step sign-in.
sessions.lesson: A stolen password works on the first try. Sign the thief out, then add a second step so the password alone is not enough.

sessions.reason: That's Anna's own computer at the office. Keep it signed in.
That's Anna's own phone. She needs it for her sign-in codes.

sessions.pick: Check each device. Which ones are really Anna's?
sessions.success: The thief is signed out, and a stolen password alone can no longer get in.
sessions.final_prompt: The thief is signed out. Now turn on 2-step sign-in so the stolen password alone cannot get back in.
sessions.final_switch: Turn on 2-step sign-in (code from Anna's phone)
sessions.final_switch_locked: Sign out every device that is not Anna's first.

network.title: Reconnect safely
network.instruction: Drag each cleared cable to the socket with the same number and shape. You can also select a cable, then a socket.
network.lesson: A cable connection is not a safety check. Keep unchecked devices disconnected until a trusted person clears them.

devices.label: ANNA'S LAPTOP
devices.note: The laptop was disconnected during the response.

devices.label: FILE SERVER
devices.note: The shared server is ready for a connection test.

devices.label: UNKNOWN DEVICE
devices.note: Nobody has confirmed that this device is safe.

network.pick: Select a device, then the matching socket.
network.unsafe: This device has not been cleared, so its plug is taped down. Leave it disconnected; reconnecting it could bring the problem back.
network.wrong: That socket has a different number or shape. Try the matching socket.
network.connected: Connected {done} of {total} cleared devices. Unchecked equipment stays offline.
network.incomplete: Connect every cleared device. Keep unchecked devices disconnected.
network.none_cleared: No device has clearance yet. Ask the response team before reconnecting anything.
network.success: Connection test passed. Only cleared devices are back online.

backup_database.title: Restore a trustworthy backup
backup_database.instruction: Inspect the cartridge labels. Choose a complete, checked copy from before the incident. Test it before restoring.
backup_database.lesson: A newer copy can contain the same problem. Check both the backup and the restored result.

backups.label: A / RECENT COPY
backups.detail:
Made after the incident.
All records copied. No passed safety check.

backups.label: B / CHECKED COPY
backups.detail:
Made before the incident.
All records copied. Safety check passed.

backups.label: C / OLDER COPY
backups.detail:
Made before the incident.
Some records are missing. Safety check incomplete.

backup_database.choose: Select a cartridge to read its label and check history.
backup_database.too_recent: This unchecked copy was made after the incident. It may contain the same problem.
backup_database.incomplete: This older copy is missing records. Being older does not make it suitable.
backup_database.unchecked: There is no passed safety check for this copy. Do not use it just because its date is earlier.
backup_database.tested: The copy is complete, checked, and from before the incident. The restore test passed.
backup_database.test_first: Test the selected copy before restoring it.
backup_database.success: Data restored from the checked copy. Visit the server terminal to verify the result.
